 Walker Kessler has only 1 rival in unique skill that’s helping Lakers surge to top of standings
 Lakers forward Jake LaRavia’s impact has been a huge catalyst behind the team’s strong start to the season.
 By David Yapkowitz • Nov 17, 2026 at 8:11 PM ET • 4 min read Add ClutchPoints on Google Ed Szczepanski-Imagn Images LOS ANGELES – The Los Angeles Lakers are tied with the San Antonio Spurs for the best record in the NBA at 12-2 . They hold the league’s second-longest current win streak at eight games, behind again, the Spurs at 12. And a big reason for the Lakers’ early success this season has been the play of Jake LaRavia .
 Jake LaRavia is in his second season with the Lakers after signing as a free agent in 2025, and he wasn’t very pleased with the way last year ended. After getting off to a strong start, he found himself mired in a shooting slump and he was ultimately benched during the Lakers’ playoff series loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder.
 Over the summer, LaRavia took it to heart and identified exactly what he needed to work on to avoid a similar let-down. But the beauty of LaRavia’s game is he can make an impact in many ways. One of the biggest areas he’s helped the Lakers with this year is with his rebounding, particularly on the offensive end . For him, making a difference on the glass comes down to studying opponents’ tendencies and adjusting game to game.
 “It’s really just all personnel-based on what team. Some teams send five guys to crash, some teams have that one crasher, it’s really just about getting hits. A lot of times you just get caught standing and watching,” LaRavia said after Lakers’ practice this past Saturday. “For me, if I stand and watch and try and out-jump someone else, I’m probably not gonna get a rebound. So you have to go and be physical and hit bodies and then just be able to dive on loose balls, finish possessions. It’s really just who is going to work harder.”
 As per the team, LaRavia is one of only nine players this season who has at least 25 offensive rebounds and 25 deflections. He has a total of 48 rebounds through 12 games, with 26 of them coming on the offensive end. During the Lakers’ win against the Bucks last Wednesday, LaRavia pulled down a career-best seven offensive boards.
 In addition to his penchant for rebounding, LaRavia has been one of the Lakers’ best defensive players. Although head coach JJ Redick singled him out recently for committing too many fouls, the former Wake Forest standout brings a unique brand of physicality and toughness on defense that pairs well with newcomers Ziaire Williams and Matisse Thybulle.
 LaRavia acknowledged that he’s among the league leaders in fouls per game (3.5, tied for sixth with VJ Edgecombe), but that he’s going to keep being aggressive defensively because that is what the Lakers need.
 “I think I’m being pretty effective. I’m gonna continue doing what I’m doing to be honest. I do play a little aggressively,” LaRavia said. “The one thing that I can change is not fouling jump shooters … just being a little less handsy and just forcing tough shots and not getting my hands involved so much. But I’m just gonna stay aggressive. I’m gonna stay physical on defense which is one of the things that makes me impactful on the court … that’s just gonna be who I am in this league.”
 LaRavia can afford to be more aggressive defensively because he has Walker Kessler behind him. Since Ziaire Williams sustained a foot injury last month, LaRavia was inserted in the starting lineup and has remained there even after Williams’ return.
 In that time, he’s had more opportunities on the court with Kessler, whom he credits with allowing him to have more defensive freedom.
 Article Continues Below “It’s great. Honestly I feel like I get on him a lot in games … you gotta give credit where credit is due. He’s a really good rim protector for us,” LaRavia said. “It makes it so much easier for aggressive and physical defenders that we can trust that we’re gonna have rim protection if we get blown by. Or we’re sending help to him and he’s gonna block the shot. So just having him on that back line is really good for us.”
 Amid the Lakers’ strong start to the year, there is still room for improvement. Redick has challenged the team to reach top-10 defensive status. They are currently 18th in opponents’ points per game (114.9) and 16th in defensive rating (115.1).
 This team has made it clear they have championship aspirations, but that isn’t going to be possible without having a top-10 ranked defense. And for LaRavia, he believes it’s doable. It’s just going to take some work and commitment.
 “Everyone’s locked in on the same goal. We want to be a good defensive team. We talk about being a top-10 defensive team in the league and we’re improving and working on it right here,” LaRavia said. “It’s just about everyone locking in and sacrificing when they get out there, playing hard. Everybody’s been in the league long enough to know that they’re gonna have to adjust their game if something’s not working out, so it’s really about going out there and playing hard.”
